chunks: Al-Ḥusayn, from Muʿallā, from Al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAbd al-Karīm, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him عليه السلام about His, the Exalted's, saying:
Then We caused those whom We chose from among Our servants to inherit the Book.

So he عليه السلام said: “What are you saying?” I said: “We say that it is regarding the Fāṭimīs.” He عليه السلام said: “It is not as you are taking it. The one who points with his sword and calls the people to opposition does not enter into this.”

So I said: “Then which one is the wrongdoer to himself?” He عليه السلام said: “The one sitting in his house who does not recognize the right of the Imam. And the moderate one is the one who recognizes the right of the Imam. And the one foremost in good deeds is the Imam.”

key_terms.السَّابِقُ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ: the one foremost in good deeds, identified here as the Imam
key_terms.الظَّالِمُ لِنَفْسِهِ: the one who wrongs himself by failing to recognize the Imam’s right
key_terms.الْفَاطِمِيِّينَ: the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام, mentioned here in a restricted interpretive context
key_terms.الْمُقْتَصِدُ: the moderate one who knows the right of the Imam
key_terms.اَلْكِتَابَ: the revealed Book inherited by those specially chosen by Allah
key_terms.اِصْطَفَيْنَا: We chose; indicating divine selection and designation
key_terms.حَقَّ الْإِمَامِ: the due right and authority of the Imam

ai.seo_question: Who are the ones chosen to inherit the Book in Qur'an 35:32 according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse about inheriting the Book as referring specifically to those chosen with true divine authority, not to everyone from the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام. It distinguishes between one ignorant of the Imam’s right, one who recognizes that right, and the Imam himself as the foremost in good deeds. The narration presents the verse as a proof for Imamate and religious authority.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn, from Moalla, from Al Washha, from Abdul Kareem, from Suleyman Bin Khalid, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the Words of the Exalted [35:32] Then We Gave the Book as an inheritance to those whom We Chose from among Our servants.

So heasws said: ‘Which thing are you saying?’ I said, ‘We are saying it is regarding the Fatimids (Descendants of Fatimaasws)’. Heasws said: ‘It isn’t where you are going. He isn’t included in this, the one who points by his sword and calls the people to opposition’. So I said, ‘Which one is the he who unjust to his own self?’

Heasws said: ‘The one seated in his house, not recognising a right of the Imamasws. And he who is moderate is the one who recognises a right of the Imamasws, and the one who is foremost in deeds of goodness is the Imamasws’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn has narrated from Mu‘alla from al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd al-Karim from Sulayman who has said that he asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the meaning of the following verse of the Holy Quran.
“We gave the book as an inheritance to Our chosen servants,.. .” [35:31]
The Imam (a.s.) asked, “What do you say about it?” I said, “We say that they are the Fatimid (descendents of Fatima, Daughter of the Holy Prophet (s.a.)”
The Imam (a.s.) said, “It is not as you say. No one who would point out his sword and call people into schism and misguidance comes in this (category of people exceeding in virtue).”

I then asked, “Who then are the ones doing wrong to themselves?” The Imam (a.s.) replied, “It is those who sit in their homes and do not know the rights of his Imam (a.s.). The moderate ones are those who know the rights of their Imam and the ones exceeding in virtue are the Imams (a.s.)”
